text:
lena: Quick dump from today's perf run on TP=8, PP=1, batch=64, seq=512. Observed a ~12% drop in tokens/s after the fp8-scaling-fix merge. Full trace attached (perfbot link).

amar: Can you paste the flame graph or the NCCL timeline? Might be an all-reduce hotspot.

lena: Flame summary: heavy time in all_reduce (NCCL) between layers 10-22. compute time per layer stable, but communication stalls increase with longer sequences. Samples: before fix 42k tok/s, after fix 37k tok/s.

carlos: That delta smells like increased comm volume or more frequent sync points. Did the fp8 patch change tensor layouts or add extra cast/dequant ops on the critical path?

lena: It added a per-shard scaling step to avoid overflow: we now run per-tensor scale+quantize before kernel, and a dequant+rescale after matmul. I thought most of that was fused but looks like TP split is forcing extra copies.

perfbot: perf trace: https://perf.internal/runs/1751004321 (timeline, nvprof, nccl-trace).

amar: Two quick angles: 1) comm/compute overlap — are kernels launched async on separate streams or blocking the default stream? 2) KV cache behavior — are we doing an AllGather of kv every forward when TP sharding changed layout?

lena: We do eager KV AllGather for attention when seq > cached_prefix, but with the fp8 change we now store cached kv as uint8 per-shard. That reduced memory but I think AllGather size stayed same because we didn't change sharding axis.

sophia: If the cache is sharded across TP dim, AllGather cost scales with TP and seq_len. For TP=8 seq=512 it's a lot. Have we measured per-step AllGather size?

carlos: I ran a quick microbench: AllGather per-step grew by ~30% after the scaling change (because we pack scale metadata per tile), which explains some of the NCCL time. Also H100 behaviour shows less slow-down vs A100, likely due to better TensorCore fp8 kernels and NCCL comm overlap.

amar: Two practical mitigations to test: 1) switch KV layout to per-gpu contiguous slices (reduces message count, increases local memory but cuts AllGather overhead). 2) use NCCL asynchronous collectives + cuda graphs so we can overlap reduce with next-layer compute.

lena: I'm worried about correctness with async lowers — fp8 quantization relies on deterministic ordering of scaling. If we overlap dequant + reduce we might see tiny nondet noise that breaks eval thresholds.

carlos: Agreed, but we can test in controlled perf branch. Suggested experiment plan:
- Baseline: current main (fp8-scaling-fix) perf profile.
- KV_layout: change to contiguous per-gpu cache (patch branch kv/contig).
- Async_reduce: enable NCCL Async AllReduce (ncclLaunch? using ncclGroupStart + streams) + pin compute on separate stream.
- FP8-fuse: try fused quant+matmul kernels (if available on H100) to eliminate explicit dequant.

amar: Pseudocode for async allreduce we used earlier:
```
// launch matmul on comp_stream
cublasGemm(..., comp_stream);
// enqueue allreduce on comm_stream
ncclAllReduce(..., comm_stream);
// make compute of next layer use comp_stream and rely on event for dependency
cudaEventRecord(evt, comm_stream);
cudaStreamWaitEvent(comp_stream, evt);
```
We need to ensure memory registration and no implicit sync with default stream.

lena: I'll try kv/contig first. If we drop AllGather bytes by 30% we might recover most of the 12% regression.

sophia: Also check kernel selection: our runtime picks different matmul kernels for fp8->fp16 path vs direct fp8 matmul. If decision heuristics use wrong input shapes (shard dims confuse them), we may be running suboptimal kernels.

carlos: Yup — I found in the profiler that GEMM path switched to a slower codelet for small M/K shapes after the patch. We should add an extra heuristic: prefer fused tf32/fp8 kernel when seq_len>256 and batch>32.

lena: Filed PERF-3421 with traces + sample config. Planning to land kv/contig branch for canary tomorrow.

amar: One more note: watch INT8 mixed experiments — scaling mismatch across tensor parallel rank leads to per-column saturation. If we use per-rank scaling, allreduce of scales is necessary or we get bias. That can add another tiny allreduce.

lena: Good catch. For now we will keep global scaling (extra allreduce) disabled unless we enforce a reduce on scale metadata once per token block. That might be cheaper than full AllGather every step.

perfbot: Action items created: PERF-3421 (trace), PERF-3422 (kv/contig experiment), PERF-3423 (async-nccl experiment).

carlos: OK let's sync tomorrow 10am. If kv/contig fixes >6% we can merge and then iterate on async overlap.

lena: Thanks all :thumbsup:

amar: thanks — will add perf test cases to the nightly matrix to catch regressions for seq=512 TP>=4.

sophia: And I'll run evals on the fp8 branch to validate no quality drop after we do overlap.

lena: Uploading raw nvprof + nccl files to the ticket now.
